content_html_sanitized:
Everything that the Prohibitionists don’t like about legal marijuana (except freedom) is actually a product of prohibition, including Big Marijuana.

See

The Shocking Truth About Big Marijuana (Weed) (Dope)

 

Obviously, in a country of 350 million people, it was inevitable that the total market for any popular consumer product would be very “Big.” That is actually a good thing because it makes it easier for the average consumer to get the best product at the best price.

 

However, that does not mean that market consolidation is inevitable.

Let’s look at different market structures in different industries.

 

First, there are natural monopolies, which usually become “utilities”, and are regulated appropriately.

 

Second, there are industries that can have economies of scale. “Beer” is an example of another popular drug. When it became possible to ship beer, or ale to larger markets, breweries became industrial in scale, but local breweries could still compete for specialty markets.

 

Now, think what America would be like if marijuana prohibition had never happened.

 

Never mind that over thirty million Americans would never have been arrested. Never mind that there would never have been established international smuggling organizations based in Mexico to bring other contraband into the United States. Never mind that sick and dying people around the world, including disabled American veterans, would not have to break the law to get relief from their suffering. Forget all that (the Prohibitionists certainly have). Let’s just “talk business”, the marijuana market.

 

In the 19th century tobacco was sold for pipes or hand rolled cigarettes, like joints. When it became possible to mass produce the modern cigarette, the same medical profession that won’t defend the right of their patients to self medicate with cannabis endorsed tobacco cigarettes on television.

 

It might seem that marijuana might follow the same model, but that would be mistaken, but not because we couldn’t find the doctors or the machines.

 

First, tobacco is much more “addictive”, requiring much higher volumes per user,

See

6 Most Addictive Drugs

 

And there is a much wider variety of strains of cannabis, like wine. The old tobacconists were more like a cannabis dispenserery.

See Alfred Dunhill

 

Of course, there will be large companies catering to the mass market. However, that is very different from limited competition and political influence over the regulators. (Regulatory capture)

 

Instead, think about “Big Hamburger”. McDonalds, or “Big Chicken”, KFC. Yes, they are very Big, but there are lots of other places that sell hamburgers or chicken, so there is still consumer sovereignty and limits on the regulatory capture that is possible.

 

So, what would “legal marijuana” look like if marijuana prohibition never happened.

 

Ironically, we can actually find an example in California during the period after the Prohibitionists had to give up on killing sick and dying people, but before the overly regulated current system was approved by the voters.

 

There were well advertised “dispensaries” everywhere in the cities. It was a lot like alcohol prohibition in New York during the Roaring Twenties. The actual medical patients could get their medicine at competitive prices from someone who might actually know something about cannabis, and it came from professional growers, maybe in Humboldt County.

See

The Decline and Fall of Humboldt County

 

But an even better example was started 50 years ago this month, the Dutch “coffee shop” system. Ironically, like the California “dispensaries”, the “coffee shops” were, and still are, technically illegal.

 

Nonetheless, there were and are a few rules. First and foremost, NO HARD DRUGS! This is called the “Separation of the Markets”.. And it works. Second, strict age limits. (Sixteen then, now eighteen.)

 

(The supply side is still technically illegal, as a result of the Dutch trying to comply with Harry Anzlinger's Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs of 1961.  But 50 years ago, almost all the cannabis was smuggled hashish.)

 

Had the US adopted the Dutch system even twenty years later, it would have made a huge difference in the structure of the US market. Instead, the US policy was just to lie about the Dutch.

 

And why not? After all, the US media would happily publish anything that the Drug Czar said.

See

The failure of Dutch drug policy " An Examination of Prohibitionist Propaganda and the Official Dutch Government Response -- Special To MarijuanaNews

 

Of course , one of the most important “features” of the CoffeeShops are tables and chairs, providing for on premises consumption, that would reduce the problem of smoking on sidewalks, etc. Instead, state regulators have treated smoking in the presence of other smokers as something to be ashamed of. Cannabis is a social drug.

See

Cannabis Prohibition: The Longest Lockdown. Social Isolation Is Harmful For Everyone

 

Ironically, “marijuana legalization” has been an economic disaster for investors, and Big Marijuana’s bank accounts are not as Big as they used to be.

 

So, what should the U.S. do?

 

The U.S. has two related  problems, Big Prohibition that wants to put the cannabis businesses out of business, and Big Contraband, that wants to keep as big a piece of the business as it possibly can. Obviously, there is a symbiotic relationship between the Prohibitionists and the Contrabandistas.

 

There is nothing that the “average person” can do about the Contrabandistas, except to struggle against their allies in Big Media, Big Government, and Big Prohibition.
